lessons.culture: A flat is described by its rooms: the living room, the bedrooms, the kitchen and the bathrooms. In old Sana'a houses the sitting room on the top floor is called the مَفْرَج. A flat can be rented furnished (فِيهَا عَفْش) or empty, so ask exactly what stays, such as the fridge, the wardrobes and the air conditioners.

lessons.culture: A small repair is often a favour between brothers, relatives or neighbours before anyone is paid, and the helper is thanked with جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا. People say الحَمْد لِلَّه when a job ends well and إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه when they promise to try. A plumber or electrician is called for bigger problems, and it is polite to ask the cost before the work starts.

lessons.culture: Neighbours matter a great deal in Yemen: they share food, visit each other when ill, keep an eye on each other's homes and try not to disturb one another with noise. Sending a dish to the new family next door is a common way to start a friendship.

challenge.title: Viewing a flat
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines in Sana'ani Arabic. You ask about a flat for rent, its bedrooms, floor and monthly rent, ask to see it, ask whether it is furnished, find the kitchen, and say that you will take it. Use at least 8 phrases from Unit 18.
required_elements: A question about the rent or the bedrooms with بِكَم or كَم.
A question about the floor, the lift or whether water and electricity are included, using فِي أَيّ or فِيه.
A request to see the flat with أَقْدَر أَبْسَر.
A question with وِين about the kitchen or the furniture.
A decision with شَاخُذهَا or أَشْتِي عَقْد إِيجَار, and a thank-you.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَدَوِّر عَلَى شَقَّة لِلإِيجَار. بِكَم الإِيجَار فِي الشَّهْر؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. adawwir 3ala shaqqa lil-iijaar. bikam al-iijaar fi sh-shahr?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I am looking for a flat to rent. How much is the monthly rent?

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. سِتِّين أَلْف رِيَال فِي الشَّهْر، وَفِيهَا ثَلَاث غُرَف نَوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. sittiin alf riyaal fi sh-shahr, wa feeha thalaath ghuraf nawm.
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Sixty thousand riyals a month, and it has three bedrooms.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.transliteration: fi ayy dawr? wa feeh miS3ad?
dialogue.english: Which floor? And is there a lift?

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: فِي الدَّوْر الثَّانِي، وَفِي العِمَارَة مِصْعَد.
dialogue.transliteration: fi d-dawr ath-thaani, wa fi l-3imaara miS3ad.
dialogue.english: On the second floor, and the building has a lift.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.transliteration: agdar abSir ash-shaqqa? wa hi mafroosha?
dialogue.english: Can I view the flat? And is it furnished?

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّل ذَلْحِين. فِيهَا عَفْش كَامِل، وَالمَطْبَخ جَنْب الصَّالَة.
dialogue.transliteration: tafaDDal dhal7een. feeha 3afsh kaamil, wa al-maTbakh janb aS-Saala.
dialogue.english: Come in now. It has full furniture, and the kitchen is next to the living room.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: Very nice. How much is the deposit?

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: إِيجَار شَهْر وَاحِد، وَتِقْدَر تَدْخُل مِنْ أَوَّل الشَّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: iijaar shahr waa7id, wa tigdar tadkhul min awwal ash-shahr.
dialogue.english: One month's rent, and you can move in from the first of the month.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.arabic: نَاهِي، شَاخُذهَا. أَشْتِي عَقْد إِيجَار لِسَنَة.
dialogue.english: OK, I will take it. I want a one-year lease.

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.english: Here are the keys to the flat. Congratulations.

dialogue.speaker: يوسف
dialogue.english: May Allah reward you with good.
